What changed and how to read this comparison

Candidate 0.34 adds 94 encoded letters for Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Turkish, Hausa, Kurdish (Kurmanji, Latin), Māori, Igbo, and Uzbek (Latin). Their pinned CLDR main, auxiliary, and index alphabets, both cases, and canonical forms are audited in every style and Latin extended subset. Turkish retains the dot in fi words; Romanian legacy cedillas use comma forms under lang="ro". Hungarian uppercase digraphs get extra clearance under lang="hu". The language selector sets the actual text language.

All 323 existing outlines and metrics, every approved pair value, and the design settings match 0.33. The foundation, numeric features, joins, and cursor stops carry forward. Baseline 0.33 lacks the new encoded letters: its language rows can use browser fallback and are not evidence of SEIReader coverage. Alphabet and shaping coverage is separate from native-reader or device certification. Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese's full encoded repertoire, and the remaining Latin alphabets come later.

Compare 20px at 1.4 and 1.5 line height, then 13/15/17px at Regular and Medium. Use Full reading width for longer lines. The sample can help identify differences; sustained reading and the readability guidance still call for feedback from readers.

Material's body-text guidance suggests around 1.5 line height. Google's web-font guide covers weight/style mapping and font loading. This page embeds the real fonts and makes no network font requests.

References: Literata 3.103 and Rubik 2.300, under the SIL Open Font License. Licenses and source hashes are kept in references/. SEIReader is an original SEIHouse design.
